body: Kyrgyzstan licence plates have a distinctive red strip. Similar plates with red strips can occasionally be found in Albania and rarely in the UAE.
Kyrgyzstan can be identified by a silver Street View car with four bars. All coverage is Generation 3. No other similar landscape countries have this car.
Kyrgyz Cyrillic script resembles Russian but includes extra characters such as Ө, Ү, Ң not found in Russian.
Kyrgyzstan coverage was taken during winter, so many trees lack leaves, landscapes are drab, and snow is visible in many areas.
In Kyrgyzstan, it is common to see trees and concrete poles painted white at the bottom.
Kyrgyzstan uses simple white bollards with diagonal black stripes near the top.
Kyrgyzstan kilometre markers feature a unique red and white triangle pattern.
Kyrgyzstan has many mosques, reflecting its Muslim majority population.
Coverage in Kyrgyzstan is limited; knowing covered roads improves location guessing.
Knowing driving directions on major roads helps narrow guesses.
The Google car’s mirror helps identify regions: in southern Kyrgyzstan, less road is visible and reflections are more diagonal compared to other areas.
West of the roundabout near Jalal-Abad, the car’s mirror often has dirt on it.
A small black dot on the car mirror indicates a specific southern region.
Divided roads mainly appear in and around Bishkek, including a major highway from Bishkek to Balykchy.
Lake Issyk Kul, Kyrgyzstan’s largest body of water, is visible north and south of the lake, sometimes obscured by buildings or trees.
Northern roads have significant snow cover and bright skies; southern roads also have snow but can be distinguished by car mirror clues.
Bishkek, the capital, is the most developed city, with many tall multi-story buildings and nearby mountains to the south.
Urban snow coverage is visible in parts of Bishkek.
Coverage south of Bishkek features hills with the Tian Shan mountains visible to the south and smog to the north due to pollution.
Towns around Bishkek have colorful utility poles painted yellow, green, white, with sometimes red tops.
Osh is the second largest city with southern mirror coverage, distinguishable from Bishkek by better weather with some clouds but never fully overcast.
In Osh, trees mostly still have their leaves, differentiating it from Bishkek in winter.
Osh city center has unique mountains topped with radio masts.
Jalal-Abad, the third largest city, has extremely overcast coverage with snowy hills to the east and is distinguished from Osh by bad weather.
Arslanbob is a snowy mountain town north of Jalal-Abad with significant elevation changes and southern mirror coverage.
Uzgen lies between Osh and Jalal-Abad, has snowy, overcast coverage and southern mirror.
In Talas, most poles are painted white at the bottom with red and yellow stripes.
Karakol city sits between snow-capped mountains; the coverage shows sunny weather and melting snow.
Naryn is characterized by a steep orange ridge to the north and large snowy mountains to the south.
The EM-04 is a major road from Bishkek to Osh, with detailed coverage including 10 location tips.
From Sokuluk to Kara Balta on EM-04, noticeable sunset coverage occurs, featuring the 'Black Dot Mirror'.
The Tian Shan mountains appear to the south of this mostly flat section of EM-04. The further from mountains, the foggier they look.
This area features steep purple/red rocky cliffs with sparse grass and shrubs, brown electricity pylons, and curved concrete guardrails.
Long stretches of snow surround hilly terrain on EM-9, except northeastern and southwestern parts in mountains.
This road section passes through rocky cliffs with spruce trees on mountainsides and blue signposts along the way.
The mostly dried Toktogul Reservoir is visible nearby, with taller mountains surrounding, greener in the south and desolate in the north.
This on-road section usually shows the Toktogul Reservoir north, amidst hilly terrain; the road here is better maintained than farther south.
EM-04 passes through a river gorge flanked by large rocky mountains, featuring overcast skies and the Naryn River to the north.
Southern road regions show extensive agriculture and vegetation, flat areas near hills, and feature the Southern Dirty Mirror.
Northern road northwest of Uzgen features overcast skies and ample snow, with the Southern Mirror.
The EM-11, or A365 in Geoguessr, runs from Bishkek to the Chinese border, marking the coverage end, with 10 associated tips.
The divided EM-11 stretch has a grassy median up to Khun-Chi.
From Khun-Chi to east of Tokmok, the road has road lines with a wide median gap.
The road lines gap narrows eastwards up to east of Kemin.
Concrete barriers replace medians from there onwards.
South of Balykchy, road becomes undivided, surrounded by dry shrublands near Chu river, with cloudy skies and nearby mountains with clouds overhead.
The dry Chu River valley features little vegetation aside from shrubs, flanked by mountains with a slightly snowy ridge to the north.
Further south, the road passes more vegetated areas with snow-capped mountains and hilly terrain, including dry hills north of Naryn.
The area beyond the valley is more vegetated with mountains and snowy peaks, while north of Naryn, it can be dry with snow in the shade.
Mountains and hills south of Naryn have a distinct mix of snow and red soil.
At-Bashi Valley has a prominent southern mountain range, scattered northern mountains, and large western hills.
EM-9 runs from Balykchy to Karakol with views of Lake Issyk Kul to the south, driving mostly east or south, featuring 3 tips.
Balykchy to Cholpon Ata features sunny weather, mountains north and lake south.
East of Cholpon Ata has overcast conditions flanked by mountains and lake with tree rows beside the road.
North of Karakol, road is flanked by tall trees and snowy mountains; weather changes around midpoint.
EM-10, or A363, connects Karakol to Balykchy, with visible Issyk Kul lake to the north, driving west, with 5 tips.
West of Karakol, road is lined with vegetation and fields, Tian Shan mountains in the distance north and south; weather clear.
Issyk Kul lake and Tian Shan mountains are often visible; landscape is sandy and rocky.
West of Fairytale Canyon shows distinct sunset coverage.
Mountains and hills to the south with some hills and Issyk Kul lake behind to the north; sandy road sides.
Western Issyk Kul area is drier and further from the road.
The EM-17 runs southeast of Talas, featuring 2 tips.
EM-17 section is very snowy with deeply slushed snow and features the Black Dot Mirror.
Further west, only southern hills have snow; landscape dry, with hills to north and south; Black Dot Mirror present.
The EM-13 is a small gravel road with limited coverage, featuring 2 tips.
East of Kazarman, EM-13 is an unpaved gravel road between hilly ridges featuring a unique towering mountain on the ridge.
Eastern EM-13 resembles western Naryn road; unpaved in Naryn valley with bushes and shrubs, recognized by white and red fences with diamond shapes.
West of Naryn, the road lies south in dry valley with hills close on the south, wide plain north, and salt-and-pepper paved texture.
East Naryn road in Naryn valley — hills close to road south, smaller plains north, unpaved parts and snow on hills parts.
M-082 road covers from Song-Kul shore to southern mountains, includes 2 tips.
Song-Kul is Kazakhstan's second major lake, with dry rolling hills and patches of snow. Covered roads are gravel.
Road south of Song-Kul is unpaved at high elevation with snowy rugged peaks and spruce trees.
M-118 runs from ski resort Arslanbob to Fergana Valley, includes 2 tips.
M-118 road features Kara Darya river in valley, is hilly and green with snow-topped distant mountains.
M118 often has snow on ground, with Babash-Ata mountain visible north, featuring Southern Dirty Mirror coverage.
M-107 is a road connecting Taskomur to Kerben; only first half covered, includes 2 tips.
M-107 section is dry and rocky with a distinctive ridge visible throughout.
Further west, M-107 passes through a hilly lush vegetated landscape with concrete barrier guardrails.
A unique road to Sary-Chelel Lake with 2 tips, featuring vegetation, poor road condition, clouds, and dead trees near Arkit.
This valley road is surrounded by buildings, dense vegetation, potholes, and darker clouds near Arkit.
Near Arkit, abundant snow and broad-leafed trees mark a distinct landscape paired with the south to north driving direction.
M-010 section bordered by spruce covered snowy mountains with snow along road sides.
A rocky dirt road to Chunkurchak is high up in snowy hills with red-tinted soil and red-and-white bollards.
Another road to the east of Chunkurchak passes through a rocky valley with snow and sparse vegetation.
Road A367 features snow-covered mountain ranges, bright southern sun, and south to north driving with the Black Dot Mirror.
Divided road north of Bishkek leading to the airport has unique yellow and black median curbs, some trees, and poles painted red and yellow at the base.
A slightly northeast-bound road north of Bishkek is recognizable from regular sunset coverage.
The road south of Jeti Oguz runs through a very green valley featuring unique orange rock formations, scattered snow, and visibility of Tian Shan mountains north and snowy mountains south.
Road north of Grigorievka passes through a rocky valley covered by spruce trees and sinuous pine forests, with little snow.
Side road north of Orto Tokoy Reservoir runs through dry mountains with sparse grass and shrubs, features a nearby mountain with little snow and a reservoir.
Remote gravel road southwest of Naryn lies in a dry, desolate valley with rocky cliff-sided mountains, scattered shrubs, and some southern snow.
